summary: Intermittent rerank 504s and result-order flips after mixed binary/JSON embedding uploads
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sporadic 504 gateway responses from /rerank and apparent non-deterministic changes in rerank ordering for the same query set. Impact: Production search UX degraded for a subset of SynthWorks customers with timeouts and inconsistent top-k. Root cause hypothesis is a format negotiation mismatch between client SDK and our ingest router leading to partial binary payloads being routed to a JSON-only consumer and to fallback CPU decoding that increases rerank latency and causes request queueing/backpressure.

Observed behavior: (1) Rerank endpoint returns 504 for ~0.8% of requests during peak, (2) When responses succeed after retries, top-5 ordering occasionally differs between retries, (3) Embeddings ingestion logs show a spike in proto-decode errors for some shard ranges coincident with increased CPU on reranker replicas.

Expected behavior: All embedding uploads should be accepted (binary or JSON) according to version negotiation; rerank should remain within latency SLO and return stable ordering for identical inputs.

Impact notes: Affects SynthWorks production clusters on dedicated capacity; visible to end users searching application knowledge base. Customer has ~1200 daily rerank calls; tail increase is driving user complaints.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use SynthWorks SDK v1.2.0 to upload embedding payloads with header 'Embedding-Version: 2026-02' and Content-Type: application/octet-stream
2) Immediately issue a /rerank call referencing the recently uploaded ids (same session) against reranker-v2 pinned model
3) Repeat at ~120 qps from a single client to simulate burst and watch for 504s and order instability
4) Alternate uploads using SDK v1.4.1 (JSON payload, application/json) to demonstrate mixed-client behavior

comments: Support (Priya): Customer reports tail latency and occasional 504s starting 2026-03-10 13:55 PST. They attached a capture of embedded payload headers. Asked for request ids and sample ids.
Customer (SynthWorks, Sean Park): Provided trace ids 9f7a2c4 and 9f7a3e1 and confirmed multiple client versions in fleet. Says rolling upgrade to SDK v1.4.1 is planned but would take 48 hours.

SRE (Ethan): Correlated trace ids to ingest-router logs. Noticed proto-decode error pattern and CPU fallback spikes on reranker instances. Hypothesis: Mixed payload encodings (binary vs json) are being routed to consumers that only accept one format; fallback decode path expensive and causes tail-timeouts.

Eng (Maya Li): Asked for minimal repro and suggested quick router tweak to accept both content-types and forward a format-hint header to downstream consumers. Opened PR 1425 to add flexible decoder and added instrumentation.

Support (Priya): Shared temporary mitigation steps with customer: increase rerank client timeout to 2s and enable client retries with idempotent backoff. Customer acknowledged and applied the change; saw drop in 504 rate to 0.1%.

SRE (Ethan): Monitoring shows queue length decreased after client retries; still seeing occasional decode failures for older SDKs. Plan is to deploy patch to ingest-router and a graceful decoder to serving runtime in staging tomorrow.
investigation_notes: - Trace 9f7a2c4: embedding payload arrived with Content-Type application/octet-stream and header Embedding-Version: 2026-02; ingest-router forwarded to shard that had JSON-only consumer due to recent rollout mismatch.
- Binary payloads are currently supported, but a recent consumer rollout removed protobuf decoder to optimize for JSON; router lacked content-negotiation enforcement leading to misroutes.
- CPU-decode fallback path in reranker is single-threaded and expensive: observed 120ms median decode vs 6ms for native consumer path under load.
- When fallback spikes, request queue builds and API gateway times out after 900ms (configured).
- Reproduced locally by running mixed-client simulator; adding 10% binary payloads at 150 qps reproduces 504 tail and top-k non-determinism.
- Related to older issue SUP-91455 where embed schema negotiation was flaky across rollout windows.
resolution: Workaround applied: Customer increased client timeout and enabled retries, reducing immediate 504s. Engineering action: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-service/pull/1425 merges a tolerant decoder and router content-negotiation fix. Planned deploy to staging 2026-03-13, canary to prod 2026-03-14 with rate-limited rollout. Post-deploy tasks: rollback plan, run mixed-client soak test, and notify customer when canary reaches 50% of traffic. Follow-up: coordinate SDK deprecation notice for v1.2.0 and add server-side instrumentation to reject clearly incompatible payloads rather than fallback.
